symptom: Arabic heading-marker regexes (_AR_PART_RE, _AR_ARTICLE_RE) in _inject_arabic_structural_headings() and numbering_depth() are insufficient for the specific heading formats used in UAE legal documents. They require the structural word (مادة/باب/فصل/قسم/جزء) at line START, but the Docling/remote OCR output for these documents formats headings differently (numbered prefixes, inline citations, or OCR formatting that prevents line-start matching). This leaves the tree flat (depth 0-1) because md_to_tree only nests based on markdown heading levels.

This leaves the tree flat (depth 0-1) because md_to_tree only nests based on markdown heading levels.
suggested_fix: Extend _inject_arabic_structural_headings to handle additional UAE-legal heading formats: (1) numbered-prefix articles like '1. المادة' or Arabic-Indic '١. المادة', (2) parenthesized articles without the structural word at line start, (3) chapter/section words preceded by numbers/ordinals. Also expand _AR_ARTICLE_RE to match المادة in additional contexts (e.g., after bullet numbers). This needs to run both on the remote Docling service AND in client.py for remote-markdown post-processing.

symptom: No heading injection or numbering-depth recognition exists for English Book/Part/Chapter structural words, and _inject_english_article_headings only matches 'Article (N)' with parentheses, not 'Article N' without parentheses. The _NUM_PART_RE regex recognizes only German structural words (Teil/Anhang/Kapitel/Abschnitt), not their English equivalents. English legal documents using Book/Part/Chapter/Article hierarchy produce flat trees because these structural headings are never promoted from prose to markdown headings, and numbering_depth returns None for them.

suggested_fix: (1) Add _inject_english_hierarchy_headings() that promotes 'Book N'/'Part N'/'Chapter N'/'Section N' lines to '#' headings (depth 1) and 'Article N' (without parens) to '##' headings (depth 2), with the same line-start anchor and char-limit guards as the Arabic and German injectors. (2) Expand _NUM_PART_RE to include English structural words: '^(?:Teil|Anhang|Kapitel|Abschnitt|Book|Part|Chapter|Section)\b'. (3) Expand _EN_ARTICLE_PROSE_RE to also match 'Article N' without parentheses (currently only matches 'Article (N)'). (4) Add corresponding calls in pdf_to_markdown_docling() alongside existing injectors.

symptom: When the remote Docling service path is used, client.py receives raw markdown and passes it to md_to_tree WITHOUT running the heading injection chain (_inject_arabic_structural_headings, _inject_english_article_headings, _inject_german_clause_headings) or heading-depth recovery (_recover_heading_depth, _relevel_by_containment, _relevel_by_numbering). These run ONLY inside pdf_to_markdown_docling() in converters.py. The remote Docling service should run its own copy of this chain, but if the remote service has a stale build (the B1-C1 issue from RFC-034 identified stale builds until 2026-08-07), or if the remote service does not include the latest heading injection improvements, the returned markdown will lack promoted headings and depth recovery, producing flat trees.

suggested_fix: Add a post-processing step in client.py's remote path (after receiving markdown from the remote service, before feeding to md_to_tree) that runs _inject_arabic_structural_headings + _inject_english_article_headings + _inject_german_clause_headings + _pre_inference_normalize + _recover_heading_depth on the received markdown. This ensures heading injection runs regardless of the remote service's build version. Alternatively, confirm the remote service has the latest code and add version-gated fallback.

symptom: _word_has_reversed_morphology (helpers.py:1232) min word length raised from 2 to 4 chars by RFC-034 D7, combined with _arabic_readability_score returning 0 for garbled/fragmented Arabic text (no common-word matches), makes _tree_is_rtl_reversed and _check_bidi_coherence gates ineffective for سياسة حوكمة's garbling pattern. Short reversed Arabic words (2-3 chars) are skipped, and readability score comparisons produce 0==0 (no difference detected). Meanwhile _is_garbled_blob's single-letter fragment check (line 910-920) should be the backstop but the stored text likely has multi-char reversed words (not literal single-char tokens), bypassing the >40% single-char ratio threshold. validate_tree returns (True,'') and classify_verdict stores PASS despite 79-100% of nodes being garbled.

suggested_fix: Lower _word_has_reversed_morphology min word length from 4 to 3, or add a dedicated garble gate prong in validate_tree that detects the specific pattern: per-node Arabic text where >50% of words have zero forward joins (indicating character-level reversal or fragmentation) even when they don't individually trigger _is_garbled_blob. symptom: classify_verdict depth threshold is a binary check (depth >= 2 -> eligible for PASS) with no document-complexity awareness. Haftpflicht-Allgemeine-Bedingungen has depth=2 and 136 nodes, which meets the code threshold, but the tree is structurally inadequate for a deeply structured German insurance document (should have Bedingungen/Abschnitt/Paragraf hierarchy). The Run 16 PASS was an LLM judge reclassification (watermark false-positive); Run 18's MARGINAL reflects the LLM judge being stricter about depth adequacy. The automated stored verdict is likely PASS or MARGINAL-from-leaf-concentration (if max_leaf_ratio > 0.30), not MARGINAL-from-depth. No code change caused this regression -- it is LLM judge scoring inconsistency surfacing a pre-existing classify_verdict threshold gap.

doc: وارد رقم 597 من مكتب أبوظبي التنفيذي بشأن التعقيب على مرئيات حكومة أبوظبي حول برنامج مهارات المهن الحرفية - Copy.pdf
symptom: RFC-034 D7 replaced the non-functional _word_has_reversed_morphology (presentation-form check with 0% TPR after NFKC normalization) with a functional joining-type-based check (_arabic_word_joins). This makes the morphological_reversal prong in _tree_is_rtl_reversed actually fire on NFKC-normalized Arabic text. For ward-597 — a document with a known corrupt numeric-junk text layer where Docling emits no full-page Picture region for Arabic body pages (RFC-028 D5 residual gap) — the newly functional detector correctly identifies RTL reversal. The repair path (reconstruct_bidi_order) fails to converge because the underlying text is too damaged (near-zero Arabic chars, all numeric junk), and the RFC-033 D8 flat-path fallback also cannot recover non-reversed content. The gate correctly rejects the document as ERROR. This is a TRUE POSITIVE — the document was always corrupt; the gate was previously blind to it (0% TPR). The comparison doc سياسة حوكمة is NOT caught by _tree_is_rtl_reversed because its corruption pattern (single-letter Arabic fragments) is different from ward-597's (numeric-junk with reversed morphology); سياسة حوكمة's gate blind spot persists as a separate known issue (RFC-034 D21/RFC-033 D2 Part B).

suggested_fix: No code fix needed for the gate itself — the D7 change is correct and the rejection is a true positive. The underlying issue is that ward-597 needs a full-page OCR fallback for scanned Arabic pages where Docling detects no Picture region (RFC-028 D5 out-of-scope residual). Until that is implemented, this document will remain at ERROR. If the goal is to recover it: implement a page-level OCR escalation path that rasterizes and OCR's full pages when no Picture region covers the Arabic body text (medium-large effort, tracked as a known gap since RFC-028).

symptom: RFC-034 D18 write barrier introduces PersistenceNotVisibleError - a new unhandled exception type in the save_doc/save_doc_meta persistence path. For world-stats-pocketbook (292 pages, ~2M chars tree producing ~5-10MB JSON), MinIO stat_object verification after put_object may exceed the 4-retry backoff window (0.1+0.3+1.0+3.0=4.4s). If raised from save_doc, it propagates as generic Exception through converters_cli, killing the child process. The doc ends up absent because save_doc_meta never executes. In preprocess_client path, error is printed and swallowed (no Redis record). This is a new failure mode introduced by commit 932d634.
